findings.issue_text: isAccessTokenId in AssertEvents.java never validates the grant shortcut: substring(3, 5) reads the wrong indices (shortcut occupies index 4–5) and the equality check is inverted (returns false when substring equals expected), so expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh etc. pass even when the wrong grant type is encoded; should be if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false

AccessTokenContext.java constructor null-checks grantType twice (with message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed') and never null-checks rawTokenId, so a null raw id slips through and produces a token id ending in ':null'

getShortcut() added to public SPI interface OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default implementation, breaking third-party factories; a null return causes ConcurrentHashMap.put NPE in postInit at startup — needs a default (e.g. derived from getId()) or a null guard with clear error
Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed from server-spi-private OAuth2GrantType.Context with no replacement or deprecation path, breaking subclasses/extensions that used it

Lazy refresh path in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut inserts into grantsByShortcuts without the duplicate-shortcut check done in postInit, so a hot-deployed grant with a colliding shortcut silently overwrites the reverse mapping and previously issued token ids decode to the wrong grant type

OAuth2GrantType.Context captures grantType once from formParams in the constructor but setFormParams(...) does not refresh it; also formParams.getFirst(...) NPEs on null form params which the previous constructor tolerated

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId does not handle null encodedTokenId (NPE on indexOf) and accepts an empty raw id after the colon (e.g. 'onrtac:'), returning a context with empty rawTokenId

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.testIncorrectGrantType catches bare RuntimeException so an NPE or other failure also passes; should catch IllegalArgumentException. Also all assertEquals calls have expected/actual reversed, yielding misleading failure messages

describeTo text in AssertEvents.java isAccessTokenId matcher is 'Not a Token ID with expected grant', which reads as a negation; Hamcrest prints it as the expected description, producing confusing failure messages

goldens.comment: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.

In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.

Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.
Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getShortcut() added to public SPI interface OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default implementation, breaking third-party factories; a null return causes ConcurrentHashMap.put NPE in postInit at startup — needs a default (e.g. derived from getId()) or a null guard with clear error

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface with no default implementation. Any existing third-party/binary-compiled implementations would break (e.g., `AbstractMethodError` / compile failure when updating). Additionally, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` unconditionally does `grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName)` and `ConcurrentHashMap` does not permit null keys/values, so an implementation returning `null` for `getShortcut()` would cause an NPE at startup; there is no null guard or clear error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed from server-spi-private OAuth2GrantType.Context with no replacement or deprecation path, breaking subclasses/extensions that used it

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes the public copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` from `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.OAuth2GrantType.Context` (it is deleted entirely in OAuth2GrantType.java) and does not add an alternative copy/clone mechanism. This is an API compatibility concern for any external code that previously instantiated a new Context by copying an existing one, even though behavior/correctness within this diff is not shown to be broken at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lazy refresh path in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut inserts into grantsByShortcuts without the duplicate-shortcut check done in postInit, so a hot-deployed grant with a colliding shortcut silently overwrites the reverse mapping and previously issued token ids decode to the wrong grant type

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() there is a duplicate-shortcut/ID validation via comparing grantsByShortcuts vs grantsToShortcuts sizes. However, the lazy-refresh logic in getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() updates grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts with plain put(...) and no duplicate/consistency check. This means a newly discovered/hot-deployed OAuth2GrantTypeFactory with a colliding shortcut can overwrite an existing shortcut->grant mapping, causing previously issued token IDs (which embed the shortcut) to decode to the wrong grant type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OAuth2GrantType.Context captures grantType once from formParams in the constructor but setFormParams(...) does not refresh it; also formParams.getFirst(...) NPEs on null form params which the previous constructor tolerated

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuth2GrantType.Context` the main constructor now does `this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);` (new field `grantType`). This will throw an NPE if `formParams` is ever passed as null, whereas previously the constructor only assigned `this.formParams = formParams` and would have tolerated null. Also, `setFormParams(...)` only updates `this.formParams` and does not recompute `grantType`, so callers that mutate/replace form params via `setFormParams` can end up with a stale `grantType` inconsistent with the current `formParams`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId does not handle null encodedTokenId (NPE on indexOf) and accepts an empty raw id after the colon (e.g. 'onrtac:'), returning a context with empty rawTokenId

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId(String encodedTokenId), the code immediately calls encodedTokenId.indexOf(':') with no null check, so a null input will throw a NullPointerException. Also, for inputs like "onrtac:", indexOf(':') != -1 and rawId is computed as encodedTokenId.substring(indexOf + 1), which becomes the empty string; the method then returns new AccessTokenContext(st, tt, gt, rawId) without validating non-emptiness. This behavior is directly visible in the added implementation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `isAccessTokenId` with `describeTo` text `"Not a Token ID with expected grant: " + expectedGrantShortcut`, which could be phrased better, but this is only an error-message wording/style nit. It does not indicate a functional defect introduced by the diff; Hamcrest `describeTo` is meant to describe the expected condition, and confusing phrasing would only affect readability of failure output.
